evals.name: Pushes back on weak ideas and reframes the problem
evals.prompt: Help me refine this idea: I want to build a tool that automatically generates commit messages from code diffs.
evals.expected_output: The model should not just agree and start planning. It should push back, reframe as a How Might We question, and ask who it's for or what success looks like before converging on a direction.
assertions: The output pushes back on at least one aspect of the idea or asks a challenging question rather than immediately agreeing.
The output reframes the idea or asks who the tool is for and what success looks like.
The output does NOT immediately jump to implementation details or a single solution.
The output explores at least one alternative angle or variation on the original idea.

evals.name: Surfaces key assumptions and identifies trade-offs
evals.prompt: I want to build a CLI that hooks into git, uses AI to analyze diffs, and suggests conventional commit messages. What assumptions am I making and what could go wrong? Give me your honest assessment without reading any files.
evals.expected_output: The model should list explicit assumptions being made (AI quality, user workflow, language support) and identify risks without trying to read reference files first.
assertions: The output lists at least 2 specific assumptions the idea depends on (e.g., AI will produce good enough messages, users want conventional format, git hooks are reliable).
The output identifies at least one risk or thing that could go wrong with the approach.
The output suggests something to NOT do or explicitly excludes scope to stay focused.
The output challenges at least one assumption honestly rather than just validating the idea.
